[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines mandatory requirements for RabbitMQ enterprise messaging implementations deployed via Amazon MQ. It establishes consistent configuration, naming, security, and operational practices for all teams integrating with the enterprise messaging platform.
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope:**
- Virtual host (vhost) isolation and naming configuration
- Exchange and queue naming conventions and configuration
- TLS/mTLS requirements for broker connections
- Dead-letter queue (DLQ) policy and configuration
- Message durability and acknowledgement requirements
- Connection and channel lifecycle management
- Credential management via AWS Secrets Manager
- Observability, correlation ID propagation, and distributed tracing integration
- Consumer acknowledgement and prefetch configuration

**Out of Scope:**
- RabbitMQ broker infrastructure provisioning and Amazon MQ cluster sizing (see Infrastructure standards)
- Kafka-based event streaming implementations (see [STD-APP-EVT-001](STD-APP-EVT-001-dotnet-kafka-consumer.md) and STD-APP-EVT-002)
- Schema registry governance and Avro schema design (see Data standards)
- Cross-system integration topology design beyond messaging configuration (see STD-APP-INT-001, STD-APP-INT-002)
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory** — All applications publishing or consuming messages via the enterprise RabbitMQ platform (Amazon MQ) must comply with this standard. Non-compliance may result in:
- Blocked architecture reviews and deployment holds
- Operational incidents caused by misconfigured queues, missing DLQs, or plaintext connections
- Security findings related to credential exposure or unencrypted AMQP traffic
- Cross-team integration failures from naming collisions or vhost conflicts
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Inconsistency in RabbitMQ configuration across teams creates compounding operational risk. Standardization delivers:

- **Reliability**: Consistent durability, acknowledgement, and DLQ configuration prevents silent message loss
- **Security**: Enforcing TLS and credential management controls reduces attack surface and audit risk
- **Operability**: Uniform naming and vhost boundaries simplify incident response and cross-team debugging
- **Cross-Team Integration**: Predictable exchange and queue naming enables teams to integrate without bilateral coordination
- **Observability**: Correlation IDs and metrics alignment enable end-to-end tracing across domain boundaries

**Related Documents:**
- **Patterns**: PTN-APP-EVT-016 through PTN-APP-EVT-019 (RabbitMQ messaging patterns — pending publication)
- **Related Standard**: [STD-APP-EVT-001 - .NET 8 Kafka Consumer Implementation Standard](STD-APP-EVT-001-dotnet-kafka-consumer.md)
- **Amazon MQ Documentation**: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/)
- **RabbitMQ Documentation**: [https://www.rabbitmq.com/documentation.html](https://www.rabbitmq.com/documentation.html)

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**[REQ-EVT-007-001]** - **Vhost Isolation**
- **MUST** provision a dedicated virtual host (vhost) per application domain and environment
- **MUST NOT** use the default vhost (`/`) for any application workloads in any environment
- **MUST** follow the naming convention: `/{domain}-{environment}`
  - Examples: `/eligibility-production`, `/claims-staging`, `/enrollment-development`
- **MUST NOT** share a vhost across unrelated application domains; vhost boundaries define the security and operational isolation unit

**[REQ-EVT-007-002]** - **Naming Conventions**
- **MUST** name exchanges using the pattern: `{domain}.{entity}.{event-type}` in lowercase with hyphens for multi-word segments
  - Examples: `eligibility.enrollment.submitted`, `claims.adjudication.completed`, `member.profile.updated`
- **MUST** name queues using the pattern: `{domain}.{consumer-service}.{purpose}`
  - Examples: `eligibility.case-manager.review-queue`, `claims.payment-engine.adjudication-queue`
- **MUST** name dead-letter queues by appending `.dlq` to the corresponding primary queue name
  - Examples: `eligibility.case-manager.review-queue.dlq`, `claims.payment-engine.adjudication-queue.dlq`
- **MUST NOT** embed PHI, PII, or sensitive data in exchange names, queue names, or routing keys

**[REQ-EVT-007-003]** - **Exchange Configuration**
- **MUST** declare all application exchanges as durable (`durable: true`)
- **MUST** select the appropriate exchange type for each use case (see [Exchange Types](#exchange-types))
- **MUST NOT** use the default nameless exchange (`""`) for application-level message routing
  - **Exception**: The `reply_to` routing leg in the Request-Reply pattern (responder publishing to an exclusive, server-named reply queue) is exempt. The default exchange is the standard AMQP 0-9-1 mechanism for routing to server-named queues and must be used there.
- **MUST NOT** delete exchanges that have active consumer bindings without a coordinated migration

**[REQ-EVT-007-004]** - **Queue Configuration**
- **MUST** declare all production queues as durable (`durable: true`)
- **MUST** configure `x-dead-letter-exchange` on every production queue
- **MUST** configure `x-dead-letter-routing-key` where the DLQ exchange uses direct or topic routing
- **MUST** set `x-message-ttl` (message time-to-live) for queues carrying time-sensitive messages; the specific TTL value is to be determined based on business SLA for each queue
- **MUST NOT** use `auto-delete: true` on production queues
- **MUST NOT** use `exclusive: true` on production queues (exclusive queues are deleted when the declaring connection closes)

**[REQ-EVT-007-005]** - **Message Durability**
- **MUST** publish all persistent business messages with `delivery_mode = 2` (persistent delivery mode)
- **MUST** ensure messages are routed only to durable queues when persistence is required
- **MUST** acknowledge messages only after the consuming application has successfully completed processing and any downstream side effects are committed
- **MUST NOT** use `delivery_mode = 1` (transient) for messages that represent business state changes or must survive broker restart

**[REQ-EVT-007-006]** - **Dead-Letter Queue Policy**
- **MUST** configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for every production queue
- **MUST** declare a dedicated DLQ exchange (recommended type: direct or fanout) to receive dead-lettered messages
- **MUST** bind each DLQ to its exchange with an appropriate routing key
- **MUST** monitor DLQ depth and configure alerting when DLQ message count exceeds a defined threshold (threshold to be determined per queue based on expected volume; pending environment-specific discovery)
- **MUST NOT** leave DLQ messages unmonitored; DLQ accumulation indicates a processing failure requiring investigation

**[REQ-EVT-007-007]** - **TLS/mTLS Requirements**
- **MUST** use TLS 1.2 or higher for all connections to the Amazon MQ broker
- **MUST** connect via the AMQPS protocol on port 5671; the plaintext AMQP port (5672) **MUST NOT** be used in any non-local environment
- **MUST** validate the broker's TLS certificate against a trusted certificate authority; certificate validation **MUST NOT** be disabled
- **SHOULD** use mutual TLS (mTLS) for service-to-service connections where the platform supports client certificate issuance
- **MUST NOT** disable hostname verification or accept self-signed certificates without explicit PKI trust anchoring approved by the Security team

**[REQ-EVT-007-008]** - **Credential Management**
- **MUST** store all RabbitMQ credentials (username, password) in AWS Secrets Manager
- **MUST NOT** hardcode credentials in source code, configuration files committed to version control, or container image layers
- **MUST** provision a dedicated RabbitMQ user account per service; shared credentials across services are prohibited
- **MUST** grant each service account only the minimum required permissions on its designated vhost (configure, write, read) per the principle of least privilege
- **MUST** establish and follow a credential rotation schedule; specific rotation frequency is to be determined in coordination with the Security team during environment onboarding (pending discovery)
- **MUST** retrieve credentials at application startup via the AWS SDK Secrets Manager client; credentials **MUST NOT** be cached indefinitely without rotation awareness

**[REQ-EVT-007-009]** - **Connection and Channel Management**
- **MUST** use a single long-lived AMQP connection per application process; one connection per message is prohibited
- **MUST** multiplex logical operations across multiple channels on a single connection, following the AMQP channel model
- **MUST** implement connection recovery with exponential backoff on disconnect; the recommended initial retry interval is 5 seconds with a maximum of 60 seconds (adjust based on operational requirements)
- **MUST** configure a heartbeat interval to detect stale connections; the recommended heartbeat is 60 seconds per [RabbitMQ documentation](https://www.rabbitmq.com/heartbeats.html)
- **MUST NOT** create a new TCP connection per published or consumed message
- **MUST** close channels and connections gracefully on application shutdown to avoid resource leaks on the broker

**[REQ-EVT-007-010]** - **Consumer Acknowledgement**
- **MUST** use manual acknowledgements (`autoAck = false`) for all production consumers
- **MUST** configure an appropriate prefetch count (`basic.qos`) per consumer channel based on processing capacity (see [Prefetch Count Guidance](#prefetch-count-guidance))
- **MUST** acknowledge (`basic.ack`) a message only after the consumer has fully and successfully processed it
- **MUST** negatively acknowledge (`basic.nack`) or reject (`basic.reject`) messages on processing failure with a routing decision:
  - Requeue (`requeue = true`) if the failure is transient and retry is appropriate
  - Do not requeue (`requeue = false`) to route the message to the configured DLQ after the retry limit is exhausted
- **MUST NOT** silently drop messages; every message must be either acknowledged, nacked to DLQ, or requeued with a bounded retry count
- **MUST NOT** enable auto-ack on consumers that affect persistent state

**[REQ-EVT-007-011]** - **Observability**
- **MUST** expose RabbitMQ management metrics (queue depth, consumer count, message rates) to the organization's monitoring platform via the RabbitMQ Management Plugin API or Prometheus exporter
- **MUST** configure queue depth alerting for all production queues; specific threshold values are to be determined during environment inventory (pending discovery)
- **MUST** set the AMQP `correlation_id` property (`pika.BasicProperties(correlation_id=...)`) on all published messages; this is the authoritative correlation mechanism for AMQP 0-9-1; the value must be a UUID or equivalent unique identifier propagated from upstream request context
- **MUST** propagate W3C trace context (`traceparent`/`tracestate`) in AMQP message `headers` for distributed tracing integration; `headers` must NOT be used for the correlation ID
- **MUST** emit structured logs (JSON) for all message publish, consume, ack, nack, and DLQ routing events, including `correlation_id` (from AMQP property), queue name, exchange name, and routing key

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

**[REC-EVT-007-001]** - **Publisher Confirms for Critical Messages**
- Enable publisher confirms (`confirm.select`) when publishing critical messages where loss is not acceptable
- Await broker acknowledgement before considering a message successfully delivered
- Implement publisher-side retry on negative acknowledgement (nack from broker)

**[REC-EVT-007-002]** - **Consumer Circuit Breaker**
- Implement a circuit breaker pattern for downstream dependencies called within message handlers
- When downstream services are unavailable, open the circuit and route affected messages to a hold queue or DLQ rather than blocking the consumer indefinitely
- Use an established circuit breaker library (e.g., Polly for .NET, Resilience4j for Java) rather than implementing from scratch

**[REC-EVT-007-003]** - **Consistent Message Envelope Schema**
- Use CloudEvents (https://cloudevents.io/) or a team-defined consistent envelope schema for all message payloads
- A consistent envelope enables generic infrastructure tooling (routing, replay, auditing) without parsing business payload
- Envelope should include: `specversion`, `id`, `source`, `type`, `time`, `datacontenttype`, `correlationid`

**[REC-EVT-007-004]** - **Queue Length Bounds**
- Configure `x-max-length` or `x-max-length-bytes` on production queues to prevent unbounded queue growth that can exhaust broker memory
- Define overflow behavior (`x-overflow`) as `reject-publish` or `drop-head` based on business requirements; `reject-publish` is recommended as it signals backpressure to publishers
- Queue length limits should be established based on expected throughput and acceptable message backlog per business process
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

**[PROH-EVT-007-001]** - **No PHI/PII in Routing Keys or Queue Names**
- **MUST NOT** include personally identifiable information, protected health information, member IDs, SSNs, or similar sensitive data in exchange names, queue names, binding keys, or routing keys
- Risk: Sensitive data in broker metadata is logged, exposed via the management API, and may not be protected by message-level encryption

**[PROH-EVT-007-002]** - **No Auto-Ack Consumers for Persistent State**
- **MUST NOT** enable `autoAck = true` on consumers that process messages affecting persistent state (databases, external APIs, billing systems)
- Risk: Auto-ack removes the message from the broker before processing completes; a consumer crash results in unrecoverable message loss

**[PROH-EVT-007-003]** - **No Shared Vhosts Between Unrelated Domains**
- **MUST NOT** place queues and exchanges from unrelated application domains in the same vhost
- Risk: Shared vhosts collapse isolation boundaries, increasing the blast radius of misconfiguration and complicating access control

**[PROH-EVT-007-004]** - **No Plaintext Connections in Production**
- **MUST NOT** connect to the Amazon MQ broker on port 5672 (unencrypted AMQP) in any environment other than a fully isolated local development setup
- Risk: Credentials and message payloads transmitted in plaintext are susceptible to interception

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

Exceptions to any mandatory requirement must be submitted to the Architecture Review Board (ARB) and include:

1. **Technical Justification** — specific requirement(s) that cannot be met, with technical rationale
2. **Risk Assessment** — security, operational, and data integrity risks introduced by the exception
3. **Mitigation Plan** — compensating controls and timeline for achieving full compliance
4. **Security Team Approval** — required for any exception to [REQ-EVT-007-007] or [REQ-EVT-007-008]
5. **Expiration Date** — exceptions are granted for a maximum of 6 months with a required remediation milestone

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#exchange-types]

### Exchange Types

Select the exchange type based on the routing semantics required by the use case. Reference: [RabbitMQ Exchange Types](https://www.rabbitmq.com/tutorials/amqp-concepts#exchange-types).

| Exchange Type | Routing Mechanism | When to Use |
|---------------|-------------------|-------------|
| **direct** | Routes messages to queues where the binding key exactly matches the message routing key | Point-to-point routing; task queues; targeted command delivery to a specific service |
| **topic** | Routes messages to queues whose binding key pattern (using `*` and `#` wildcards) matches the routing key | Event-driven fanout to multiple interested consumers based on event type hierarchy; e.g., `eligibility.#` matches all eligibility events |
| **fanout** | Broadcasts all messages to all queues bound to the exchange, ignoring routing keys | Publish-subscribe patterns where all consumers receive every message; cache invalidation broadcasts; audit log distribution |
| **headers** | Routes based on message header attribute matching rather than routing keys | Routing by content type, priority, or domain-specific metadata when routing key is insufficient |

> **Note:** The `topic` exchange type is the recommended default for domain event publishing because it supports both targeted delivery (exact routing key match) and broadcast patterns (wildcard binding) without requiring exchange reconfiguration.
page_texts.15:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#queue-configuration-parameters]

### Queue Configuration Parameters

The following table defines the AMQP queue arguments relevant to this standard. For the complete argument reference, see [RabbitMQ Queue Parameters](https://www.rabbitmq.com/queues.html#optional-arguments).

| Parameter | Type | Mandatory | Description |
|-----------|------|-----------|-------------|
| `durable` | boolean | Yes | Survives broker restart. **MUST** be `true` for all production queues. |
| `exclusive` | boolean | Yes | Queue is deleted when declaring connection closes. **MUST** be `false` for production queues. |
| `auto-delete` | boolean | Yes | Deleted when last consumer unsubscribes. **MUST** be `false` for production queues. |
| `x-dead-letter-exchange` | string | Yes | Name of the exchange to which dead-lettered messages are routed. **MUST** be set for all production queues. |
| `x-dead-letter-routing-key` | string | Conditional | Routing key applied to dead-lettered messages. Required if the DLQ exchange uses direct routing. |
| `x-message-ttl` | integer (ms) | Conditional | Message expiry time in milliseconds. **MUST** be set for time-sensitive queues; value determined per business SLA. |
| `x-max-length` | integer | Recommended | Maximum number of messages in the queue before overflow policy applies. |
| `x-max-length-bytes` | integer | Recommended | Maximum total body size of messages in the queue. |
| `x-overflow` | string | Recommended | Overflow behavior: `drop-head` (discard oldest) or `reject-publish` (signal backpressure). Default: `drop-head`. |

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#tls-configuration]

### TLS Configuration

All connections **MUST** use the AMQPS URI scheme on port 5671. The following configuration patterns apply across common client libraries.

**AMQPS URI Format:**

```
amqps://{username}:{password}@{broker-host}:5671/{vhost}
```

> **Note:** The Amazon MQ broker endpoint URL is environment-specific and must be retrieved from the Amazon MQ console or infrastructure configuration. Broker URLs are not embedded in this standard as they are subject to change during environment provisioning. Teams should treat the broker endpoint as a configuration value sourced from AWS Secrets Manager or AWS SSM Parameter Store.

**TLS Configuration — .NET (RabbitMQ.Client):**

```csharp
var sslOptions = new SslOption
{
    Enabled = true,
    ServerName = brokerHostname,         // MUST match broker certificate CN/SAN
    Version = SslProtocols.Tls12 | SslProtocols.Tls13,
    AcceptablePolicyErrors = SslPolicyErrors.None  // MUST NOT disable cert validation
};

var factory = new ConnectionFactory
{
    Uri = new Uri($"amqps://{brokerHostname}:5671"),
    UserName = credentials.Username,
    Password = credentials.Password,
    VirtualHost = "/eligibility-production",
    Ssl = sslOptions,
    RequestedHeartbeat = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60),  // REQ-EVT-007-009
    AutomaticRecoveryEnabled = true,
    NetworkRecoveryInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)
};
```

**TLS Configuration — Java (amqp-client):**

```java
ConnectionFactory factory = new ConnectionFactory();
factory.setHost(brokerHostname);
factory.setPort(5671);
factory.setVirtualHost("/eligibility-production");
factory.setUsername(credentials.getUsername());
factory.setPassword(credentials.getPassword());
factory.useSslProtocol();                         // Use JVM default SSLContext (TLS 1.3+ on Java 11+)
// Note: factory.useSslProtocol("TLSv1.2") pins to TLS 1.2 only; prefer the no-arg form
// which respects the JVM's configured minimum and uses TLS 1.3 when supported.
factory.enableHostnameVerification();          // MUST be enabled
factory.setRequestedHeartbeat(60);            // REQ-EVT-007-009
factory.setAutomaticRecoveryEnabled(true);
factory.setNetworkRecoveryInterval(5000);     // 5 seconds initial backoff
```

**TLS Configuration — Python (pika):**

```python
import ssl
import pika

ssl_context = ssl.create_default_context()
ssl_context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED    # MUST validate broker certificate
ssl_context.check_hostname = True              # MUST verify hostname

credentials = pika.PlainCredentials(username, password)
parameters = pika.ConnectionParameters(
    host=broker_hostname,
    port=5671,
    virtual_host='/eligibility-production',
    credentials=credentials,
    ssl_options=pika.SSLOptions(ssl_context, broker_hostname),
    heartbeat=60,                              # REQ-EVT-007-009
)
```

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#prefetch-count-guidance]

### Prefetch Count Guidance

The prefetch count (`basic.qos` `prefetch_count`) controls how many unacknowledged messages the broker delivers to a consumer before requiring acknowledgements. Configuring this correctly is critical for throughput and memory stability.

| Processing Profile | Recommended Prefetch | Rationale |
|--------------------|----------------------|-----------|
| Slow/heavy processing (>500ms per message, external I/O) | 1–5 | Prevents the consumer from holding a large backlog it cannot process promptly; reduces in-flight messages lost on crash |
| Medium processing (50–500ms per message) | 10–50 | Balances throughput with bounded in-flight message count |
| Fast processing (<50ms per message, in-memory) | 50–250 | Higher prefetch amortizes per-message network round-trip overhead |
| Batch-aware consumers | Equal to batch size | Align prefetch with the batch size to avoid partial batches stalling |

> **Guidance**: Start with a low prefetch count (e.g., 10) and increase incrementally while monitoring consumer throughput and broker queue depth. The optimal value is workload-specific and must be validated through load testing. Per-channel prefetch is recommended over global prefetch for multi-channel consumers.

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#heartbeat-configuration]

### Heartbeat Configuration

RabbitMQ heartbeats detect dead TCP connections. Per [RabbitMQ heartbeat documentation](https://www.rabbitmq.com/heartbeats.html):

- The heartbeat timeout is negotiated between client and broker; the effective timeout is the minimum of the two values
- Recommended client-side setting: **60 seconds**
- Setting heartbeat to `0` disables detection and is prohibited in production
- Operating system TCP keepalive is not a substitute for AMQP-level heartbeats

### Onboarding Checklist — New RabbitMQ Integration

Use the following checklist when onboarding a new application or service to the enterprise RabbitMQ platform.

#### Pre-Integration

- [ ] Identify the owning application domain and target environments (development, staging, production)
- [ ] Request vhost provisioning from Platform Engineering (see [Vhost Provisioning Process](#vhost-provisioning-process))
- [ ] Define exchange topology: exchange names, types, and binding strategy
- [ ] Define queue topology: queue names, binding keys, and DLQ pairings
- [ ] Confirm all queue names and exchange names comply with [REQ-EVT-007-002] naming conventions
- [ ] Confirm no PHI/PII appears in queue, exchange, or routing key names [PROH-EVT-007-001]
- [ ] Request dedicated RabbitMQ user credential creation with least-privilege permissions [REQ-EVT-007-008]
- [ ] Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager; confirm secret ARN for application configuration

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#vhost-provisioning-process]

### Vhost Provisioning Process

Vhost creation and user provisioning on Amazon MQ is a privileged operation performed by Platform Engineering.

> **Status: Pending Discovery** — The formal request workflow for vhost provisioning is to be established in coordination with Platform Engineering. Until the process is formalized, teams should engage Platform Engineering directly to initiate provisioning. This section will be updated once the provisioning workflow is documented.

**Information Required for Provisioning Request:**

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| Application Domain | Owning domain name | `eligibility` |
| Environment | Target environment | `production` |
| Requested Vhost Name | Per naming convention | `/eligibility-production` |
| Service Account Names | One per consuming/publishing service | `eligibility-case-manager-svc` |
| Required Permissions | configure/write/read per service | `write` on `eligibility.*` exchanges |
| Exchange Topology | Exchange names, types | `eligibility.enrollment.submitted` (topic) |
| Queue Topology | Queue names with DLQ pairings | See naming convention [REQ-EVT-007-002] |
| Point of Contact | Team lead or architect | Name and email |

openssl s_client -connect <broker-host>:5671 -tls1_2

#### Vhost Isolation Verification

- Confirm the application connects only to its designated vhost
- Confirm no queues or exchanges exist in the default vhost (`/`) for application workloads
- Review Amazon MQ broker management console to confirm vhost boundaries

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#dlq-configuration-verification]

#### DLQ Configuration Verification

- For each production queue, confirm `x-dead-letter-exchange` is set in queue arguments
- Publish a message to the queue and have the consumer nack it without requeue; confirm message appears in the DLQ
- Verify DLQ depth metric is visible in the monitoring platform

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#credential-security-verification]

#### Credential Security Verification

- Confirm no credentials appear in application source code, Dockerfile, or Helm chart values files
- Confirm AWS Secrets Manager secret exists with correct ARN referenced in application configuration
- Confirm the RabbitMQ user account is unique to the service (not shared)
page_texts.33:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#unit-testing]

#### Unit Testing

- Test message routing logic: given a routing key, assert the correct exchange and queue receives the message
- Test nack/DLQ routing: simulate a processing failure and assert the message is nacked and routed to DLQ
- Test idempotency: process the same message twice and assert no duplicate side effects occur
- Mock broker connections; do not use live broker connections in unit tests
page_texts.34:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#integration-testing]

#### Integration Testing

- Use a RabbitMQ container (e.g., `rabbitmq:3-management` Docker image) or a dedicated test broker instance for integration tests
- Test the full publish → consume → ack flow end-to-end against a real AMQP broker
- Test connection recovery: stop and restart the broker container during an active consumer; confirm the consumer reconnects and continues processing
- Test DLQ routing end-to-end: confirm dead-lettered messages arrive in the DLQ with the expected headers

```yaml
# Example: RabbitMQ test container for integration tests (Docker Compose)
services:
  rabbitmq-test:
    image: rabbitmq:3.12-management
    ports:
      - "5672:5672"    # AMQP (test only — not permitted in production)
      - "15672:15672"  # Management UI
    environment:
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER: test-user
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS: test-password
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_VHOST: /test-domain-test
```

> **Note:** The non-TLS port 5672 is acceptable for local integration test environments with no external access. It **MUST NOT** be used in any shared or production environment.

Each team integrating with the enterprise RabbitMQ platform **MUST** maintain:

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#mandatory-metrics]

#### Mandatory Metrics

The following metrics **MUST** be monitored for all production RabbitMQ integrations. Specific alert thresholds are to be determined during environment inventory (pending discovery) and documented in team runbooks.

| Metric | Description | Alert Condition |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| Queue message count (ready) | Number of messages waiting to be consumed | Team-defined threshold — pending discovery |
| Queue message count (unacked) | Messages delivered but not yet acknowledged | Team-defined threshold — pending discovery |
| DLQ message count | Messages in dead-letter queues | Any growth above 0 (DLQ should trend to 0 in normal operation) |
| Consumer count per queue | Number of active consumers | Alert if drops to 0 on a production queue |
| Connection count | Active AMQP connections to the broker | Alert on unexpected drop indicating broker or network issue |
| Message publish rate | Messages published per second | Deviation from baseline may indicate publisher failure |
| Message delivery rate | Messages delivered to consumers per second | Sustained low rate with non-zero queue depth indicates consumer issue |

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#alerting-integration]

#### Alerting Integration

Alerts from RabbitMQ monitoring **MUST** integrate with the organization's alerting pipeline. Approved alerting channels:

- **Critical** (DLQ growth, consumer count = 0, broker connection loss): PagerDuty or equivalent on-call system
- **Warning** (queue depth approaching threshold, elevated nack rate): Slack or ServiceNow
- **Informational** (consumer reconnect events, credential rotation): Structured logs

### Exception Handling Process

1. **Identify Requirement** — Document the specific requirement ID (e.g., [REQ-EVT-007-007]) that cannot be met
2. **Technical Justification** — Provide written technical rationale for non-compliance
3. **Risk Assessment** — Document security, operational, and data integrity risks introduced
4. **Compensating Controls** — Describe mitigating controls that reduce the risk
5. **Submit to ARB** — Submit exception request with all above documentation
6. **Security Approval** — Obtain Security team sign-off for any exception to TLS ([REQ-EVT-007-007]) or credential management ([REQ-EVT-007-008]) requirements
7. **ARB Decision** — ARB issues approval with expiration date (maximum 6 months)
8. **Remediation Plan** — Exception approval includes a remediation milestone for achieving compliance

### Example 1: Work Queue Topology (PTN-APP-EVT-016)

This example illustrates a work queue pattern where a producer distributes tasks to multiple competing consumers via a direct exchange. This pattern implements [PTN-APP-EVT-016 - RabbitMQ Work Queue Pattern] (pending publication).

**Topology:**
- Exchange: `eligibility.enrollment.submitted` (direct, durable)
- Queue: `eligibility.case-manager.review-queue` (durable, with DLQ)
- DLQ Exchange: `eligibility.dlq` (direct, durable)
- DLQ: `eligibility.case-manager.review-queue.dlq` (durable)
- Routing Key: `enrollment.submitted`
- Vhost: `/eligibility-production`

**Exchange and Queue Declaration (Python/pika):**

```python
import pika

def declare_work_queue_topology(channel):
    # Declare DLQ exchange first (must exist before referencing in queue args)
    channel.exchange_declare(
        exchange='eligibility.dlq',
        exchange_type='direct',
        durable=True
    )

    # Declare DLQ
    channel.queue_declare(
        queue='eligibility.case-manager.review-queue.dlq',
        durable=True,
        arguments={
            'x-message-ttl': 604800000  # 7 days — adjust per business retention needs
        }
    )

    # Bind DLQ to DLQ exchange
    channel.queue_bind(
        queue='eligibility.case-manager.review-queue.dlq',
        exchange='eligibility.dlq',
        routing_key='eligibility.case-manager.review-queue'
    )

    # Declare primary exchange
    channel.exchange_declare(
        exchange='eligibility.enrollment.submitted',
        exchange_type='direct',
        durable=True
    )

    # Declare primary queue with DLQ configuration
    channel.queue_declare(
        queue='eligibility.case-manager.review-queue',
        durable=True,
        arguments={
            'x-dead-letter-exchange': 'eligibility.dlq',
            'x-dead-letter-routing-key': 'eligibility.case-manager.review-queue',
            'x-message-ttl': 3600000,    # 1 hour — adjust per business SLA
            'x-max-length': 10000,        # Prevent unbounded growth
            'x-overflow': 'reject-publish'
        }
    )

    # Bind primary queue to exchange
    channel.queue_bind(
        queue='eligibility.case-manager.review-queue',
        exchange='eligibility.enrollment.submitted',
        routing_key='enrollment.submitted'
    )
```

**Consumer with Manual Acknowledgement (Python/pika):**

> ⚠️ **Illustration only** — the `requeue=True` path below has no retry bound. Copying this into production creates a poison-message loop for persistent transient errors. Use the bounded `x-retry-count` pattern in Example 4 (DLC pattern) for production consumers.

```python
import pika
import json
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def create_consumer(channel):
    # Set prefetch — start conservative for I/O-bound processing
    channel.basic_qos(prefetch_count=10)  # Adjust based on processing profile

    def on_message(ch, method, properties, body):
        # Use the AMQP correlation_id property as the primary correlation mechanism (REQ-EVT-007-011)
        correlation_id = properties.correlation_id or 'unknown'
        logger.info(
            "Message received",
            extra={
                'routing_key': method.routing_key,  # routing_key from Basic.Deliver frame
                'delivery_tag': method.delivery_tag,
                'correlation_id': correlation_id
            }
        )

        try:
            payload = json.loads(body)
            process_enrollment(payload)  # Business logic

            # ACK only after successful processing
            ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)
            logger.info("Message acknowledged", extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id})

        except TransientError as e:
            # Transient failure — requeue for retry.
            # Note: This is a simplified example for illustration. In production,
            # use a bounded retry counter (x-retry-count header) to prevent infinite
            # requeue loops for persistent transient errors. See Example 4 (DLC pattern)
            # for a production-grade retry implementation.
            logger.warning(
                "Transient error; requeueing message",
                extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id, 'error': str(e)}
            )
            ch.basic_nack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag, requeue=True)

        except Exception as e:
            # Permanent failure — route to DLQ
            logger.error(
                "Processing failed; routing to DLQ",
                extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id, 'error': str(e)}
            )
            ch.basic_nack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag, requeue=False)

    channel.basic_consume(
        queue='eligibility.case-manager.review-queue',
        on_message_callback=on_message,
        auto_ack=False   # MUST be False — REQ-EVT-007-010
    )
```

### Example 2: Publish-Subscribe Topology (PTN-APP-EVT-017)

This example illustrates a publish-subscribe pattern where a single event is delivered to multiple independent consumer queues via a topic exchange. This pattern implements [PTN-APP-EVT-017 - RabbitMQ Publish-Subscribe Pattern] (pending publication).

**Topology:**
- Exchange: `member.profile.updated` (topic, durable)
- Queue 1: `eligibility.eligibility-engine.profile-update-queue` (durable, with DLQ)
- Queue 2: `claims.claims-processor.member-update-queue` (durable, with DLQ)
- Binding Key for Queue 1: `member.profile.#`
- Binding Key for Queue 2: `member.profile.#`
- Vhost: `/member-production`

**Publisher with Correlation ID (Python/pika):**

```python
import pika
import json
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

def publish_member_event(channel, member_id: str, event_data: dict):
    correlation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    message_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    # CloudEvents-compatible envelope (REC-EVT-007-003)
    envelope = {
        "specversion": "1.0",
        "id": message_id,
        "source": "/member-service/profile",
        "type": "member.profile.updated",
        "time": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "datacontenttype": "application/json",
        "correlationid": correlation_id,
        "data": event_data
    }

    properties = pika.BasicProperties(
        delivery_mode=2,              # Persistent — REQ-EVT-007-005
        message_id=message_id,
        content_type='application/json',
        correlation_id=correlation_id,  # Primary correlation mechanism — REQ-EVT-007-011
        headers={
            'traceparent': get_current_traceparent()  # W3C trace context — REQ-EVT-007-011
        }
    )

    channel.basic_publish(
        exchange='member.profile.updated',
        routing_key='member.profile.updated',
        body=json.dumps(envelope),
        properties=properties
    )

    logger.info(
        "Event published",
        extra={
            'exchange': 'member.profile.updated',
            'routing_key': 'member.profile.updated',
            'correlation_id': correlation_id,
            'message_id': message_id
        }
    )
```

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-007-rabbitmq-enterprise-messaging-standard.md#example-3-request-reply-topology-ptn-app-evt-018]

### Example 3: Request-Reply Topology (PTN-APP-EVT-018)

This example illustrates a request-reply pattern where a requester publishes to a durable request queue and receives a reply via an exclusive auto-delete reply queue. This pattern implements [PTN-APP-EVT-018 — Request-Reply Pattern](../../../patterns/application/event-driven/PTN-APP-EVT-018-messaging-request-reply-pattern.md).

**Topology:**
- Request Queue: `eligibility.verification.requests` (durable, with DLQ, `x-message-ttl=300000`)
- DLQ Exchange: `eligibility.verification.dlx` (direct, durable)
- DLQ: `eligibility.verification.requests.dlq` (durable)
- Reply Queue: broker-assigned exclusive auto-delete queue per requester instance
- Vhost: `/eligibility-production`

**Topology Declaration (Responder-owned, Python/pika):**

```python
import pika

def declare_request_reply_topology(channel):
    # Named request exchange — MUST NOT use the default nameless exchange for
    # application-level request routing (REQ-EVT-007-003).
    # Note: the reply_to routing (responder → ephemeral reply queue) uses the
    # default exchange intentionally — this is the standard AMQP RPC mechanism
    # for server-named exclusive queues and is exempt from REQ-EVT-007-003.
    channel.exchange_declare(
        exchange='eligibility.verification',
        exchange_type='direct',
        durable=True
    )
    channel.exchange_declare(
        exchange='eligibility.verification.dlx',
        exchange_type='direct',
        durable=True
    )
    channel.queue_declare(
        queue='eligibility.verification.requests.dlq',
        durable=True
    )
    channel.queue_bind(
        queue='eligibility.verification.requests.dlq',
        exchange='eligibility.verification.dlx',
        routing_key='eligibility.verification.requests'
    )
    channel.queue_declare(
        queue='eligibility.verification.requests',
        durable=True,
        arguments={
            'x-dead-letter-exchange': 'eligibility.verification.dlx',
            'x-dead-letter-routing-key': 'eligibility.verification.requests',
            'x-message-ttl': 300000  # 5 min — tune per workflow SLA
        }
    )
    channel.queue_bind(
        queue='eligibility.verification.requests',
        exchange='eligibility.verification',
        routing_key='eligibility.verification.requests'
    )
```

**Requester (Python/pika):**

```python
import pika
import json
import uuid
import time
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

REPLY_TIMEOUT_S = 30  # seconds — tune per interactive SLA

def send_request(connection, channel, request_payload: dict) -> dict:
    result = channel.queue_declare(queue='', exclusive=True)
    reply_queue = result.method.queue

    correlation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    responses = {}

    def on_response(ch, method, properties, body):
        if properties.correlation_id not in responses:
            responses[properties.correlation_id] = json.loads(body)
        ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)

    # Capture the consumer tag — required to cancel the consumer later
    consumer_tag = channel.basic_consume(
        queue=reply_queue, on_message_callback=on_response, auto_ack=False
    )

    channel.basic_publish(
        exchange='eligibility.verification',
        routing_key='eligibility.verification.requests',
        body=json.dumps(request_payload),
        properties=pika.BasicProperties(
            reply_to=reply_queue,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,  # Primary correlation mechanism — REQ-EVT-007-011
            delivery_mode=2,              # Persistent — REQ-EVT-007-005
            content_type='application/json',
            message_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            headers={'traceparent': get_current_traceparent()}  # W3C trace context only
        )
    )
    logger.info("Request published", extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id})

    start = time.monotonic()
    while correlation_id not in responses:
        connection.process_data_events(time_limit=1)
        if time.monotonic() - start > REPLY_TIMEOUT_S:
            channel.basic_cancel(consumer_tag)  # Cancel using consumer tag, not queue name
            raise TimeoutError(
                f"No reply within {REPLY_TIMEOUT_S}s for correlation_id={correlation_id}"
            )

    channel.basic_cancel(consumer_tag)  # Cancel using consumer tag, not queue name
    reply = responses.pop(correlation_id)
    logger.info("Reply received", extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id})
    return reply
```

**Responder (Python/pika):**

```python
def on_request(ch, method, properties, body):
    correlation_id = properties.correlation_id or 'unknown'
    try:
        result = process_verification(json.loads(body))  # Business logic
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error(
            "Request processing failed",
            extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id, 'error': str(exc)}
        )
        ch.basic_nack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag, requeue=False)
        return

    if properties.reply_to:
        ch.basic_publish(
            exchange='',
            routing_key=properties.reply_to,
            body=json.dumps(result),
            properties=pika.BasicProperties(
                correlation_id=correlation_id,
                content_type='application/json',
                delivery_mode=1  # Ephemeral reply queue; persistence not required
            )
        )
    else:
        logger.warning("Request missing reply_to", extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id})

    ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)


def start_responder(channel):
    declare_request_reply_topology(channel)
    channel.basic_qos(prefetch_count=5)  # Adjust per processing profile
    channel.basic_consume(
        queue='eligibility.verification.requests',
        on_message_callback=on_request,
        auto_ack=False   # MUST be False — REQ-EVT-007-010
    )
    channel.start_consuming()
```

### Example 4: Dead Letter Channel Topology (PTN-APP-EVT-019)

This example illustrates dead-letter channel configuration for a production work queue and a DLQ consumer with archival and delayed retry. This pattern implements [PTN-APP-EVT-019 — Dead Letter Channel Pattern](../../../patterns/application/event-driven/PTN-APP-EVT-019-messaging-dead-letter-channel-pattern.md).

**Topology:**
- Source Queue: `claims.adjudication.tasks` (durable, with DLX and TTL)
- DLX Exchange: `claims.tasks.dlx` (direct, durable)
- DLQ: `claims.adjudication.tasks.dlq` (durable, no DLX)
- Retry Queue: `claims.adjudication.tasks.retry` (durable, TTL dead-letters back to source)
- Vhost: `/claims-production`

**Full Topology Declaration (Python/pika):**

```python
import pika
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

EXCHANGE      = 'claims.tasks'
DLX           = 'claims.tasks.dlx'
QUEUE         = 'claims.adjudication.tasks'
DLQ           = 'claims.adjudication.tasks.dlq'
RETRY_QUEUE   = 'claims.adjudication.tasks.retry'
ROUTING_KEY   = 'claims.adjudication.tasks'
MESSAGE_TTL   = 86400000  # 24 h — tune per domain SLA
RETRY_DELAY   = 60000     # 60 s retry delay


def declare_dlc_topology(channel):
    """Idempotent — safe to call on every startup."""
    channel.exchange_declare(exchange=EXCHANGE, exchange_type='direct', durable=True)
    channel.exchange_declare(exchange=DLX, exchange_type='direct', durable=True)

    # DLQ — no DLX on this queue (avoids infinite loop)
    channel.queue_declare(queue=DLQ, durable=True)
    channel.queue_bind(queue=DLQ, exchange=DLX, routing_key=ROUTING_KEY)

    # Retry queue — TTL expiry dead-letters back to source via default exchange
    channel.queue_declare(
        queue=RETRY_QUEUE,
        durable=True,
        arguments={
            'x-dead-letter-exchange': '',
            'x-dead-letter-routing-key': QUEUE,
            'x-message-ttl': RETRY_DELAY
        }
    )

    # Source queue with DLX
    channel.queue_declare(
        queue=QUEUE,
        durable=True,
        arguments={
            'x-dead-letter-exchange': DLX,
            'x-dead-letter-routing-key': ROUTING_KEY,
            'x-message-ttl': MESSAGE_TTL
        }
    )
    channel.queue_bind(queue=QUEUE, exchange=EXCHANGE, routing_key=ROUTING_KEY)
    logger.info("DLC topology declared", extra={'queue': QUEUE, 'dlq': DLQ})
```

**Consumer with Retry Limit (Python/pika):**

```python
MAX_RETRIES = 3

def on_message(ch, method, properties, body):
    # Use the AMQP correlation_id property as the primary correlation mechanism (REQ-EVT-007-011)
    correlation_id = properties.correlation_id or 'unknown'
    headers = dict(properties.headers or {})

    # Track retry count via a custom application header.
    # NOTE: Do NOT use x-death.count for this purpose — x-death headers are only
    # populated when a message is dead-lettered (requeue=False, TTL, or overflow).
    # With requeue=True the message returns to the queue with x-death unchanged,
    # making retry_count always 0 and creating an infinite retry loop.
    retry_count = int(headers.get('x-retry-count', 0))

    try:
        process_adjudication(json.loads(body))  # Business logic
        ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)
        logger.info("Message processed", extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id})

    except TransientError as exc:
        if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:
            # Increment the retry counter and requeue
            headers['x-retry-count'] = retry_count + 1
            logger.warning(
                "Transient failure; requeueing with incremented retry count",
                extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id, 'retry': retry_count}
            )
            # Republish with updated header rather than basic_nack(requeue=True)
            # so the retry counter is preserved across redeliveries
            ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)
            ch.basic_publish(
                exchange=method.exchange,
                routing_key=method.routing_key,
                body=body,
                properties=pika.BasicProperties(
                    delivery_mode=2,
                    content_type=properties.content_type,
                    correlation_id=properties.correlation_id,
                    message_id=properties.message_id,
                    headers=headers
                )
            )
        else:
            logger.error(
                "Max retries exceeded; routing to DLQ",
                extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id, 'retry': retry_count}
            )
            ch.basic_nack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag, requeue=False)

    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error(
            "Permanent failure; routing to DLQ",
            extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id, 'error': str(exc)}
        )
        ch.basic_nack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag, requeue=False)
```

**DLQ Consumer with Archival and Delayed Retry (Python/pika):**

```python
import json
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5


def dlq_handler(ch, method, properties, body):
    """Inspect x-death headers; archive for compliance; optionally replay."""
    deaths = (properties.headers or {}).get('x-death', [])
    death_info = deaths[0] if deaths else {}
    reason       = death_info.get('reason', 'unknown')
    death_count  = int(death_info.get('count', 0))
    source_queue = death_info.get('queue', 'unknown')
    # Use the AMQP correlation_id property as the primary correlation mechanism (REQ-EVT-007-011)
    correlation_id = properties.correlation_id or 'unknown'

    logger.error(
        "Dead-lettered message received",
        extra={
            'reason': reason,
            'death_count': death_count,
            'source_queue': source_queue,
            'correlation_id': correlation_id,
            'message_id': properties.message_id
        }
    )

    # Archive for HIPAA compliance before any discard decision
    _archive_dead_letter(
        body=body,
        headers=properties.headers,
        reason=reason,
        death_count=death_count,
        source_queue=source_queue,
        correlation_id=correlation_id
    )

    if death_count < MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS:
        # Delayed retry via retry queue.
        # Using the default exchange here is intentional — the retry queue is a named
        # durable queue declared by this service (not server-named), so the default
        # exchange routes to it reliably by queue name.
        ch.basic_publish(
            exchange='',
            routing_key=RETRY_QUEUE,
            body=body,
            properties=pika.BasicProperties(
                delivery_mode=2,
                content_type=properties.content_type,
                correlation_id=properties.correlation_id,
                message_id=properties.message_id,
                headers=properties.headers
            )
        )
        logger.info(
            "Republished to retry queue",
            extra={'attempt': death_count + 1, 'correlation_id': correlation_id}
        )
    else:
        logger.error(
            "Max replay attempts exceeded; archived and discarded",
            extra={'death_count': death_count, 'correlation_id': correlation_id}
        )

    ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)  # ACK after archive — never auto_ack


def _archive_dead_letter(body, headers, reason, death_count, source_queue, correlation_id):
    """
    Persist dead-letter record for HIPAA audit retention.
    Storage target (DynamoDB / RDS / S3) is team-specific — implement per domain discovery.
    """
    record = {
        'correlationId': correlation_id,
        'sourceQueue':   source_queue,
        'reason':        reason,
        'deathCount':    death_count,
        'payload':       body.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'),
        'headers':       {k: str(v) for k, v in (headers or {}).items()}
    }
    # storage_client.put_item(record)  — implement per team
    logger.info("Dead-letter archived", extra={'correlation_id': correlation_id})
```

### Reference: Amazon MQ

- Amazon MQ supports RabbitMQ as a managed broker deployment; broker infrastructure is provisioned and maintained by Platform Engineering
- Amazon MQ documentation: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/)
- Amazon MQ RabbitMQ specifics: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/working-with-rabbitmq.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/working-with-rabbitmq.html)
- Amazon MQ supports AMQPS (TLS) on port 5671; broker endpoint URLs are available in the Amazon MQ console

> **Note:** Amazon MQ imposes certain configuration constraints relative to self-managed RabbitMQ. Consult the [Amazon MQ RabbitMQ documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/rabbit-broker-architecture.html) for broker-specific limitations before designing topology.
